source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect real-time data: Establish continuous monitoring systems like air-quality sensors and emission monitors to capture real-time data on the types and amounts of pollutants emitted. Make sure the monitors are regularly calibrated and maintained for accuracy.

3. Identify parameters to monitor: Document all relevant pollutants known to be emitted by the industry, such as particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and any industry-specific hazardous air pollutants (HAPs).

4. Record metadata: Include details on the type of sensors used, their location, the date and time of data collection, operative conditions during measurement (e.g., weather conditions), and any maintenance or calibration updates.

5. Track the source of emissions: Categorize emissions based on the source within the facility, such as stacks, vents, and fugitive emissions from leaking valves or storage
